summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM deployments scale, enabling teams to trace prompt behavior, track token costs, detect quality regressions, and debug agent failures in production. The LLM observability platform market reached an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and is projected to hit $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, with Gartner predicting it will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on cost overruns, hallucinations, and latency spikes that directly impact user experience and infrastructure budgets.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, agent reasoning loops, prompt inputs/outputs, evaluation runs, and dataset management primarily within the LangChain ecosystem
features: Rich trace visualization with step-by-step chain debugging
Built-in evaluation framework with human and automated scoring
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overages around $2.50 per 1,000 traces; Enterprise custom pricing. Approximately £80/month for 100K traces.
tools.best_for: Teams heavily invested in the LangChain ecosystem who need the richest debugging and evaluation framework with minimal setup friction

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per call, latency, prompt templates, and model performance across multiple providers via a proxy gateway
features: Best-in-class cost tracking and spend dashboards
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
tools.pricing: Hobby tier free at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (SOC-2 and HIPAA); Enterprise custom. Approximately £20/month for 100K traces.
tools.best_for: Cost-sensitive teams needing the simplest possible setup with best-in-class cost visibility and multi-provider support without vendor lock-in

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiment runs, model evaluation metrics, prompt iterations, dataset versions, and end-to-end ML pipeline lineage
features: Experiment tracking with rich comparison dashboards
Weave module for LLM-specific tracing and evaluation
Collaborative annotation and human feedback tools
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50/seat/month; Enterprise custom pricing. Usage-based storage and compute costs apply at scale.
tools.best_for: ML-focused teams that need to bridge traditional model experimentation with LLM evaluation, particularly those already using W&B for training workflows

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM spans and traces, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline quality, embedding drift, model performance, hallucination signals, and enterprise telemetry at scale
features: Extends long-standing ML monitoring into LLM workloads
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and self-hostable for free; Arize managed platform has a free tier with limited volume; Growth and Enterprise plans are custom-priced based on data volume and features.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing robust telemetry, RAG quality monitoring, and ML-to-LLM observability continuity with strong OpenTelemetry compatibility

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, cost, custom evaluation scores, user sessions, and feedback signals across any LLM framework
features: Detailed LLM tracing with nested span support
Prompt management with versioning and A/B testing
Custom score hooks for evaluation integration
SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and REST API
Integration with DeepEval and other evaluation libraries
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud plans from approximately £20/month for 500K requests; Self-hosted free (infrastructure costs approximately £30/month with ~2 hours maintenance/month); Enterprise custom.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open-source flexibility with production-grade tracing and prompt management, especially those preferring self-hosting or OpenTelemetry-native workflows

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token counts, latency, and model metadata via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation across any provider or framework
features: Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and more
Sends traces to any OTel-compatible backend (Jaeger, Grafana, Datadog, etc.)
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free; backend storage and infrastructure costs depend on chosen destination (e.g., self-hosted Jaeger is free, Datadog adds per-host costs).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with existing OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want to add LLM observability without adopting a new proprietary platform or changing their current monitoring stack

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination rates, answer relevancy, contextual precision and recall, toxicity, bias, and 50+ evaluation metrics in production and CI/CD pipelines
features: Online production evaluations integrated into the observability layer
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft teams
RAG evaluation metrics including contextual recall and precision
Combines evaluation depth with trace monitoring
tools.pricing: DeepEval open-source library is free; Confident AI managed platform has a free tier; Pro and Enterprise plans are custom-priced based on evaluation volume and team size.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing evaluation-first observability who need the deepest quality metrics coverage in production, especially for RAG systems and safety-critical applications

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, and completions alongside full infrastructure metrics, logs, distributed traces, and frontend Real User Monitoring (RUM) in a unified platform
features: Unified LLM and infrastructure observability in a single deployment
Logs, metrics, traces, and RUM in one tool
Eliminates need for a separate DevOps telemetry stack
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free; Cloud managed plan starts with a free tier; paid plans scale by data ingestion volume with competitive per-GB pricing; Enterprise custom.
tools.best_for: DevOps and platform teams tired of managing separate LLM observability and infrastructure monitoring stacks who want a single unified deployment covering all telemetry types

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: Tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so identical or near-identical prompts return cached responses without hitting the LLM API, which can reduce redundant call costs by 20-40% in applications with repetitive query patterns.

Right-size your model selection per task: Use smaller, cheaper models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku) for simple classification or extraction tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, using observability tools to trace which calls actually require high-capability models versus which are over-provisioned.

Set token budget limits and monitor prompt length drift: Use observability dashboards to track average input and output token counts over time — prompt length often creeps upward as context is added, so alerting on per-call token thresholds and trimming system prompts or retrieved context chunks can yield significant savings at scale.

Use evaluation data to reduce retry and fallback waste: Poor prompt quality leads to retries, re-rankings, and multi-call agent loops that multiply API costs; running offline evaluations with tools like DeepEval or Langfuse's score hooks helps you catch low-quality prompt templates before they hit production and generate expensive failed call chains.
